claims.text: OpenAI launched Codex on May 16, 2025 as a research preview: a cloud-based software engineering agent that works on many tasks in parallel, powered by codex-1.

codex-1 is a version of OpenAI o3 optimized for software engineering, trained with reinforcement learning on real-world coding tasks to mirror human style and PR preferences, follow instructions precisely, and iteratively run tests until they pass.
Each Codex task runs in its own isolated cloud sandbox environment preloaded with the user's repository.
Within a Codex sandbox, the agent can read and edit files and run commands including test harnesses, linters, and type checkers.
Codex tasks typically take between 1 and 30 minutes depending on complexity, and users can monitor progress in real time.

After finishing a task, Codex commits its changes in its environment and cites terminal logs and test outputs as verifiable evidence; users can then request revisions, open a GitHub pull request, or integrate changes locally.
AGENTS.md files placed in a repository are text files, akin to README.md, that tell Codex how to navigate the codebase, which commands to run for testing, and how to follow project practices.
At launch, OpenAI stated that users must still manually review and validate all agent-generated code before integration; Codex reports uncertainty and test failures explicitly.
On OpenAI's internal SWE task benchmark, codex-1 scored 75%, versus 70% for o3-high, 67% for o4-mini-high, and 11% for o1-high.
codex-1 was evaluated on SWE-Bench Verified at a maximum context length of 192k tokens and medium reasoning effort, excluding 23 samples that were not runnable on OpenAI's internal infrastructure.
On June 3, 2025, OpenAI made Codex available to ChatGPT Plus users and added the option to give Codex internet access during task execution.
In Codex cloud mode, network access is disabled by default to reduce supply-chain risk, according to DeepStation citing OpenAI's o3/o4-mini Codex system card addendum.

The Codex CLI offers three approval levels: Suggest (default, approve each edit and command), Auto Edit (applies file changes but prompts before shell commands), and Full Auto (runs autonomously in a sandboxed, network-disabled workspace).

An OpenAI team built and shipped an internal beta product with 0 lines of manually written code over five months, starting from an empty repository in late August 2025; they estimate it took about 1/10th the time of writing by hand.
The OpenAI harness-engineering experiment produced roughly a million lines of code and about 1,500 merged pull requests from three engineers initially, averaging 3.5 PRs per engineer per day.
In the OpenAI experiment, throughput per engineer increased as the team grew from three to seven engineers.
The initial scaffold (repo structure, CI config, formatting rules, package manager setup, app framework) and the first AGENTS.md were generated by Codex CLI using GPT-5.

OpenAI's team had Codex review its own changes locally, request additional agent reviews locally and in the cloud, respond to feedback, and iterate until all agent reviewers were satisfied; humans may review PRs but are not required to, with almost all review effort pushed agent-to-agent.
OpenAI's team reported early progress was slower than expected because the environment was underspecified, and that their bottleneck became human QA capacity as code throughput increased.

To make the app legible to Codex, OpenAI made it bootable per git worktree, wired the Chrome DevTools Protocol into the agent runtime, and exposed logs, metrics, and traces through an ephemeral local observability stack per worktree.

At the February 2, 2026 Codex app launch, OpenAI reported that overall Codex usage had doubled since the December 2025 GPT-5.2-Codex release and that over 1,000,000 developers had used it in the preceding month.

OpenAI relaunched Codex cloud at DevDay on September 29, 2026: users publish a reusable environment once and every task starts from that prepared filesystem in its own isolated workspace; the earlier architecture is labeled Codex Cloud (Legacy) and still powers code review and GitHub, GitLab (beta), and Linear integrations.

OpenAI's Codex Cloud docs say each task has its own workspace and can keep working while the user's computer is asleep, with results reviewed as changed files and checks, follow-up requests, and commits or pull requests.
The Codex Cloud environment settings shown in OpenAI's docs include a Network setting (for example 'Package managers'), plus repositories, secrets, install script, and start skill.
